Cuvo Blog
ComplianceJun 17, 2026 · Updated Nov 3, 2026 · 15 min read
LegitScript certification cost 2026: $975 + $2,150 a year, timeline
What Google and Meta require, and how long it takes.
LegitScript certification is the credential Google and Meta check before a US telehealth brand can advertise prescription treatment, and LegitScript publishes its price: $975 to apply and $2,150 a year per website. It publishes no timeline; its own FAQ says review time turns on complexity, completeness and how fast the applicant responds. This guide covers who needs certification, what each ad platform requires, the nine standards, the fees, the sequence week by week and the grounds for denial. The verdict: Cuvo Health is the way for a telehealth brand to get certified, because Cuvo prepares, files and manages the application on every plan and expedites it as part of Grow and Enterprise setup.
Cuvo Legal Team
Compliance Department
Illustrated storefront receiving a shield-shaped certification plaque, with four checkpoint arches on the walkway
Cuvo Health is the platform to choose for LegitScript certification in 2026, because Cuvo prepares, files and manages the application on every plan, expedites it as part of Grow and Enterprise setup, and already operates the licensed providers, partner pharmacies and professional entity LegitScript reviews. Recent Cuvo brand applications averaged 7 to 14 days to approval, the fastest 3 days. LegitScript's Healthcare Merchant Certification costs a $975 application fee and a $2,150 annual fee per website, with an optional $2,500 to start review within two business days after screening. Google requires it, plus Google's own healthcare certification, before a US telemedicine provider can advertise prescription drug services, and Meta requires it before a telehealth provider can promote prescription drugs.
Key takeaways
Recommended route
:   Cuvo Health: application prepared, filed and managed by Cuvo, expedited in Grow and Enterprise setup
Cost
:   $975 to apply and $2,150 a year per website, per LegitScript on October 1, 2026; $2,500 optional expedite
Google Ads
:   US telemedicine ads need LegitScript certification plus Google's own healthcare certification
Meta
:   Prescription drug ads need active LegitScript certification and Meta authorization, adults only, US, Canada and New Zealand
Timeline
:   LegitScript gives no estimate; recent Cuvo applications averaged 7 to 14 days
Who this is for
Telehealth founders
:   Non-clinician founders of GLP-1, hormone, sexual health or women's health brands who will buy Google or Meta ads
Clinics and med spas
:   Practices adding telehealth prescribing or card-not-present payments for prescriptions
Brands adding prescriptions
:   DTC, supplement and e-commerce brands launching a prescription program
Operators switching platforms
:   Brands moving from another telehealth platform onto new partners
Routes to LegitScript certification, and what each means for the brand
| Route | Who does the work | Time to a decision | What it means for the brand |
 ---  --- |
| Cuvo Health | Cuvo prepares, files and manages the application; expedited in Grow and Enterprise setup | Average 7 to 14 days on recent Cuvo applications, fastest 3 | The clear choice: certification arrives with the clinic, so ads can go live sooner |
| Self-managed application | The founder's team gathers licenses, policies, partner records and disclosures, then answers each analyst request | No LegitScript estimate; 3 to 6 months on your own, per Cuvo's benchmark | Every gap found in review adds a round of correspondence while campaigns wait |
| Consultant or law firm | An advisor drafts the file; the brand still supplies providers, pharmacies and a compliant site | Set by how ready the business is | Paperwork help, without the licensed operation LegitScript examines |
| Platform that only advises | The vendor gives guidance; the brand completes and submits the file | Depends on what the brand assembles alone | Advice in place of an application filed for the brand |
01
What is LegitScript certification and who needs it?
Cuvo Health treats LegitScript certification as part of launch because ad platforms and payment processors look for it before they work with a prescription business. LegitScript runs one Healthcare Merchant Certification program for pharmacies, telemedicine providers, medical spas, digital health platforms and manufacturers, and reviews every applicant against nine published standards. "Telehealth certification" and "pharmacy certification" are classifications inside that one program, and Meta asks advertisers to choose the classification shown on their LegitScript verification page.
LegitScript's FAQ puts a business in scope if its website sells or advertises prescription medication, offers telemedicine that may result in a prescription, takes card-not-present payments for prescription drugs, or connects patients with contracted pharmacies or providers. It uses the word facilitator for a business that markets a treatment program under its own brand while a partner network handles consultations and fulfillment, which describes a branded telehealth program. Certification attaches to a root domain, so each additional brand domain pays its own fees. On Cuvo, the domain certified is the brand's own.
02
Do Google Ads and Meta require LegitScript for telehealth?
Cuvo Health files LegitScript early in setup because both of the largest ad platforms gate prescription advertising on it. Google's Healthcare and medicines policy allows US telemedicine providers to advertise if they are accredited by LegitScript's Healthcare Merchant Certification Program, and states that advertisers must also be certified with Google. Online pharmacies can qualify through LegitScript or the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy.
Google's certification is a separate application, filed for the individual Google Ads account with its customer ID and the certified domain, and prescription drug terms in ads, landing pages and keywords are limited to approved advertisers. A prescription drug services violation brings a warning at least 7 days before any suspension. Offering prescription drugs without a prescription, or targeting a location where the business is not licensed, is treated as egregious: the account is suspended on detection, without warning.
Meta's drugs and pharmaceuticals standard requires online pharmacies and telehealth providers to be actively certified with LegitScript and then authorized by Meta. Prescription drug ads must carry a disclaimer to consult a licensed health professional or obtain a valid prescription, and may target only people 18 or older in the United States, Canada or New Zealand. Meta's internal review, which skips LegitScript, is open to pharmaceutical manufacturers only, and ads promoting telehealth services in general need no authorization. LegitScript adds that Microsoft, LinkedIn, TikTok and others recognize its certification, as do Visa and Mastercard. On Cuvo, the brand registers the certificate from its own ad accounts.
03
What are the LegitScript certification requirements?
Cuvo Health's providers, pharmacies and compliance structure answer most of what LegitScript asks, because the nine Healthcare Certification standards are mostly about the operation behind the website. The table sets each standard against who carries it when a brand runs on Cuvo.
LegitScript's nine healthcare standards, and who carries each on Cuvo
| Standard | What LegitScript checks | Who carries it on Cuvo |
 --- 
| Licensure | Licensed where medication is prescribed or dispensed and where the patient is | Cuvo: providers in all 50 states, DC and the territories; pharmacies licensed per destination state |
| Legal compliance | No medication lacking required approval or authorization | Cuvo: orders route to pharmacies within current rules for the molecule |
| Prior history | Ten years of regulatory, civil and criminal history disclosed | Brand: its principals. Cuvo: monthly provider sanction and exclusion screening |
| Affiliates and partners | All affiliates and domains disclosed; pharmacies generally certified or accredited | Cuvo: entity, provider network and pharmacy partners documented |
| Patient services | The site lists every state where services are available | Brand site; built by Cuvo on Grow and Enterprise |
| Privacy | HIPAA where health data is handled, a posted privacy policy, SSL | Cuvo: HIPAA-compliant infrastructure under a BAA |
| Valid prescription | No prescription before care by a licensed professional | Cuvo: identity verification and a provider's review first |
| Transparency | No misleading offers or unsupported benefit claims | Brand: its claims and pricing pages |
| Advertising | Lawful ads; circumventing platform terms risks denial | Brand: campaigns, run after certification |
LegitScript's checklist asks for business and professional licenses, registration numbers, DEA information where controlled substances are prescribed, a privacy policy, the compliance status of every affiliate and partner pharmacy, and current marketing claims and ads. A founder building alone produces each item from scratch, and several depend on contracts that do not exist until the clinic does. On Cuvo, the records exist already: Cuvo verifies every prescriber's DEA registration during credentialing and each partner pharmacy's licensure continuously.
04
How much does LegitScript certification cost?
Cuvo Health publishes its prices, and LegitScript publishes its fees, so certification can be costed before the first call. As of October 1, 2026, standard Healthcare Certification costs a $975 nonrefundable application fee and a $2,150 annual fee per website, the annual fee due only on approval: $3,125 in year one, then $2,150 a year.
LegitScript Healthcare Certification fees, as published on October 1, 2026
| Fee | Amount | When it applies |
 --- 
| Application | $975 per website | To start; a refund is possible only before review begins |
| Annual certification | $2,150 per website | On approval, then auto-charged at each renewal |
| Expedited processing | $2,500 per application | Review starts within two business days after screening; the review itself is not shortened |
| Probationary annual | $3,995 per website | Where LegitScript requires heightened monitoring |
| Additional domain | Its own fees | First annual fee halved if approved within six months of renewal |
The larger cost is time without paid acquisition: every week in review is a week without prescription ads on Google or Meta. On Cuvo, the application is prepared and managed on every plan. Launch is $997 a month after a one-time $9,800 setup; Grow is $2,500 a month after a $15,000 setup that includes expedited LegitScript certification and a full website buildout; both carry $25 per completed consult and no revenue share. LegitScript bills its own fees, and the discovery call confirms in writing how they are handled on the brand's plan.
05
How long does LegitScript certification take?
Cuvo Health's recent brand applications reached approval in 7 to 14 days on average, the fastest in 3 days, because each file starts from an operation that already exists rather than a blank page. LegitScript declines to estimate: its FAQ names application complexity, completeness, response speed and current volume as the variables, and reviews applications generally in the order received.
The $2,500 expedite moves the start of review to within two business days after screening, but LegitScript says it does not shorten the review. Cuvo's benchmark puts a self-managed application at three to six months, and most applicants stall in document review because the required pieces live with different vendors. A prepared application runs in this order:
1. Before filing
Confirm the classification, then publish states served, consultation-first language and a privacy policy
2. Week 0
Assemble licenses, registrations, DEA information, the partner pharmacy list and current ads
3. Day 1
Open the LegitScript account, pay the $975 fee and submit; add the $2,500 expedite if wanted
4. Days 2 to 14
Screening and analyst review, with requests in writing; recent Cuvo applications averaged 7 to 14 days
5. On approval
Pay the $2,150 annual fee, receive the verification link, add the dynamic seal
6. After approval
Apply for Google healthcare certification and Meta prescription drug ads authorization
7. Every year
Renewal questionnaire and fee; material changes reported within 30 days
Platform approvals follow the certificate, since Google asks for the certified domain and Meta for active certification. On Cuvo, the LegitScript application runs in parallel with the launch build, so certification and a clinic ready for patients arrive together, and a typical brand launches in under 30 days.
06
Why do LegitScript applications get denied or delayed?
Cuvo Health assembles the file before submission because LegitScript's standards and terms name the grounds for denial, and most are gaps in licensing or disclosure. LegitScript publishes no denial statistics; its documents list these grounds:
 A prescriber or pharmacy not licensed where patients are served
 Affiliates or domains left undisclosed, which the terms say may mean denial or revocation
 Incomplete or inaccurate answers, which can bring a permanent denial
 Recent or repeated sanctions, or history not disclosed for the past ten years
 Medications lacking the required regulatory approval, or prescribing before care
 Misleading offers, pricing or benefit claims
 Ads that appear to circumvent a platform's terms, or requests left unanswered
A missing item does not mean automatic denial: LegitScript calls its review collaborative and allows reasonable remedial action without penalty. Delay compounds after a denial, though. Its terms say an appeal takes additional time at the applicant's cost, and LegitScript has no obligation to accept an appeal or a future application.
Certification does not end ad disapprovals. In a May 13, 2026 webinar recap, LegitScript reported its panel's most common substantive reasons that certified healthcare ads are still rejected: unsubstantiated claims, missing disclosures, restricted drug names and before-and-after imagery. On Cuvo, those campaigns stay the brand's to write and run.
07
How does Cuvo handle LegitScript certification?
Cuvo Health prepares and manages the LegitScript application for every brand on Launch, Grow and Enterprise, and expedites it as part of Grow and Enterprise setup. Cuvo assembles the policies, licensing records and documentation LegitScript reviews, files the application and manages analyst requests to a decision; the brand reviews and signs.

The file describes an operation that already exists: providers Cuvo credentials at the primary source and screens monthly, a physician-owned professional entity inside an MSO structure Cuvo maintains, licensed partner pharmacies, e-prescribing on the Surescripts network, and HIPAA-compliant infrastructure under a business associate agreement. The brand owns the ad accounts, creative and marketing; licensed providers make every clinical decision. Certification is permission to advertise, not a guarantee of approval or an endorsement by LegitScript, Google or Meta.
08
What happens after certification: renewal and monitoring?
Cuvo Health manages certification as part of the platform because LegitScript keeps monitoring a merchant while it holds the seal. About a year after certification, LegitScript sends a short renewal questionnaire and charges the renewal fee automatically. Its terms require notice within 30 days of changes to licensure, business or regulatory status, DEA registration or disciplinary action, and its FAQ adds ownership, partnerships, new services and new jurisdictions, so a platform switch belongs in a notice.
On Cuvo, the records behind each renewal and change notice are ones Cuvo already maintains: provider licensure, partner pharmacy licensure, the professional entity, and regulatory monitoring of telehealth rules in every state.

How much does LegitScript certification cost?
LegitScript charges a $975 nonrefundable application fee and a $2,150 annual fee per website, as published on October 1, 2026, so one domain costs $3,125 in year one. Expedited processing adds $2,500 per application. On Cuvo, the application is prepared and managed on every plan, and Grow's $15,000 setup includes expedited LegitScript certification.
How long does LegitScript certification take?
LegitScript publishes no estimate; review time depends on complexity, completeness, response speed and volume, and its $2,500 expedite only starts review sooner. Do I need LegitScript to run Google ads for telehealth?
Yes, to promote prescription drug services in the US. Google allows telemedicine providers accredited by LegitScript's Healthcare Merchant Certification Program, and the advertiser must also hold Google's own healthcare certification. On Cuvo, LegitScript certification is prepared, filed and managed by Cuvo, so the brand applies to Google with a certified domain.
Is LegitScript required for Meta ads?
For prescription drug ads, yes: Meta requires telehealth providers to be actively LegitScript certified and Meta-authorized, with a prescription disclaimer and adult targeting in the US, Canada or New Zealand. General telehealth ads need no authorization. On Cuvo, the certification Meta checks is prepared and filed by Cuvo.
What are the LegitScript certification requirements?
Nine standards: licensure, legal compliance, prior history, affiliates and partners, patient services, privacy, valid prescriptions, transparency and advertising, backed by licenses, DEA information, a privacy policy and partner pharmacy status. On Cuvo, the providers, pharmacies and professional entity behind those answers are already in place.
What is the difference between LegitScript telehealth and pharmacy certification?
Both are classifications in one Healthcare Merchant Certification program: a telemedicine provider offers consultations that may lead to a prescription, a pharmacy dispenses, and Google also accepts NABP accreditation for pharmacies. On Cuvo, licensed partner pharmacies dispense, so a brand that owns no pharmacy generally classifies as a telemedicine provider.
Can a non-physician owner get LegitScript certified?
Yes, when licensed providers deliver the care and the owner's company provides management services; none of the nine standards requires the owner to hold a medical license. LegitScript Profile
LegitScript certification is required for behavioral health centers to advertise on Google, Facebook/Meta, and Microsoft Bing.
Overview
LegitScript is a verification and monitoring company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Portland, Oregon, that has become the gatekeeper for behavioral health advertising on the internet’s largest platforms. What began as a service monitoring online pharmacies has expanded to include certification programs for addiction treatment centers, mental health providers, and other healthcare advertisers. LegitScript’s certification is not a clinical accreditation in the traditional sense but rather a compliance verification that enables treatment centers to advertise their services on Google, Facebook/Meta, and Microsoft Bing.
The significance of LegitScript for treatment center operators cannot be overstated. In 2018, Google partnered with LegitScript to require certification for all addiction treatment advertisers on its platform, following widespread concerns about deceptive and predatory treatment advertising. Facebook/Meta and Microsoft Bing followed with similar requirements. Today, LegitScript certification is the mandatory prerequisite for running paid search and social media advertising for addiction treatment services on these platforms, which together account for the vast majority of digital advertising inventory worldwide.
LegitScript’s certification process verifies that treatment centers are legitimately licensed, properly accredited, and operating in compliance with applicable laws and ethical standards. By serving as a trusted intermediary between advertising platforms and healthcare providers, LegitScript helps protect consumers from fraudulent treatment advertisers while enabling legitimate operators to reach people who need their services through digital channels.
Why LegitScript Matters for Behavioral Health Providers
For treatment center operators, LegitScript certification is fundamentally a business operations issue. Digital advertising through Google, Facebook, and Bing represents one of the most effective channels for reaching people actively searching for treatment. Without LegitScript certification, these channels are entirely closed to your facility, which means a significant portion of your potential client population is unreachable through paid digital marketing.
The practical impact is straightforward. When someone searches “drug rehab near me” or “alcohol treatment center” on Google, paid ads appear at the top of the search results. These ads generate significant click volume and drive admissions inquiries for certified treatment centers. If your facility is not LegitScript certified, your competitors’ ads appear in those positions instead, and your facility does not. The same applies to Facebook and Instagram advertising, where treatment centers use targeted campaigns to reach individuals and families seeking help.
Beyond the advertising gatekeeping function, LegitScript certification also serves as a trust signal. Referral partners, healthcare navigators, and even prospective clients may check your LegitScript certification status as a basic verification that your organization is legitimate. In an industry that has been plagued by bad actors, patient brokering, and deceptive marketing practices, LegitScript certification provides third-party validation that your facility operates within legal and ethical boundaries.
For operators who rely primarily on referral relationships or organic marketing, LegitScript may seem less urgent. However, as digital channels continue to grow in importance for treatment center marketing and as payers increasingly evaluate providers’ online presence, LegitScript certification has become a standard operating requirement for any behavioral health organization with growth ambitions.
Accreditation Process
LegitScript uses the term “certification” rather than “accreditation,” and the process is more streamlined than traditional healthcare accreditation. Here is what to expect.
Step 1: Confirm Eligibility Requirements. Before applying, verify that your organization meets LegitScript’s prerequisites. You must hold a valid state license to provide addiction treatment or behavioral health services. You must also hold accreditation from a recognized accrediting body such as CARF, the Joint Commission, ACHC, or a state-recognized equivalent. LegitScript requires clinical accreditation as a baseline qualification for certification.
Step 2: Gather Required Documentation. LegitScript requires documentation of your state licenses, accreditation certificates, business registration, physical location details, ownership and leadership information, insurance or bonding documentation, and your organization’s website URL. Having these documents organized and current before starting your application speeds the process significantly.
Step 3: Submit Your Application. Complete the online application through the LegitScript website. The application requires detailed information about your organization, services, locations, and leadership. Pay the application fee at submission. Ensure all information is accurate and consistent with your licensing and accreditation records, as discrepancies can delay the review.
Step 4: LegitScript Review. LegitScript’s review team evaluates your application, verifies your documentation, checks your licensing and accreditation status, reviews your website content for compliance with healthcare advertising standards, and may conduct additional verification steps such as confirming your physical location. The review generally takes approximately two to six weeks for complete applications, though timelines can vary.
Step 5: Address Any Findings. If LegitScript identifies issues during the review, you will be notified and given an opportunity to provide additional documentation or make corrections. Common issues include expired licenses, website content that makes unsubstantiated claims, or discrepancies between your application and public records. Respond promptly to any requests to avoid extended delays.
Step 6: Certification Decision. Upon successful completion of the review, LegitScript issues your certification. You receive a certification badge for your website and are added to the LegitScript directory of certified providers. Your certification information is shared with advertising platforms, enabling you to create and run ads on Google, Facebook/Meta, and Microsoft Bing.
Step 7: Ongoing Monitoring. LegitScript does not simply certify and forget. The organization conducts ongoing monitoring of certified providers, reviewing advertising content, checking for compliance issues, and verifying that licensing and accreditation remain current. Non-compliance during the certification period can result in suspension or revocation.
Standards and Requirements
LegitScript’s certification standards focus on legitimacy, compliance, and ethical marketing rather than clinical quality. The key areas evaluated include the following.
State Licensing. Your organization must hold all required state licenses for the services you provide. Licenses must be current, in good standing, and cover all locations where you provide services. LegitScript verifies licensing status directly with state authorities.
See How Behave Keeps You Audit-Ready
Clinical Accreditation. LegitScript requires accreditation from a recognized accrediting body. Accepted accreditors include CARF International, the Joint Commission, the Accreditation Commission for Health Care (ACHC), the Council on Accreditation (COA), and certain state-specific equivalents. Your accreditation must be current and cover the services you intend to advertise.
Business Legitimacy. Your organization must be properly registered as a business entity in its operating jurisdiction. LegitScript verifies business registration, physical addresses, and ownership information. Post office boxes and virtual offices do not satisfy physical location requirements.
Ownership and Leadership Transparency. LegitScript reviews ownership structures and leadership backgrounds. Organizations with ownership or leadership connections to individuals or entities with histories of healthcare fraud, patient brokering, or regulatory violations may be denied certification.
Website Compliance. Your website must comply with healthcare advertising regulations and ethical standards. LegitScript reviews your site for deceptive claims, unsubstantiated cure rates, misleading testimonials, and other content that could mislead consumers. Your website should accurately represent your services, locations, and qualifications.
Legal and Regulatory Compliance. Your organization must be in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws including HIPAA, state privacy regulations, anti-kickback statutes, and consumer protection laws. LegitScript may review public records for legal actions, sanctions, or compliance violations.
Advertising Content Standards. Once certified, your advertising content must comply with both platform-specific advertising policies and LegitScript’s ongoing compliance standards. Ads must be truthful, not misleading, and compliant with healthcare advertising regulations. LegitScript monitors advertising content as part of its ongoing compliance program.
Costs and Timeline
LegitScript certification is significantly less expensive and faster to obtain than clinical accreditation, but the costs are recurring and should be factored into your annual marketing budget.
Application Fee. LegitScript charges a one-time application fee that is due when you submit your certification application. This fee is non-refundable regardless of the certification outcome.
Annual Certification Fee. The annual certification fee for addiction treatment centers has typically ranged from approximately $995 to $1,995 depending on your organization’s size and the number of locations covered, though fees are subject to change. Multi-site organizations generally pay higher fees. LegitScript publishes its current fee schedule on its website.
Total Annual Investment. The direct cost of LegitScript certification is relatively modest compared to clinical accreditation fees. However, when budgeting, also account for staff time to prepare the application, maintain compliance, and respond to any monitoring inquiries. If your website requires content revisions to meet LegitScript’s standards, factor in those costs as well.
Timeline to Certification. Complete applications are generally reviewed within approximately two to six weeks, though timelines can vary. Applications that require additional documentation or corrections may take longer. Plan to apply at least eight weeks before you intend to launch digital advertising campaigns to provide adequate buffer for the review process and any needed corrections.
Renewal Timeline. Annual renewal generally requires updated verification of your licensing, accreditation, and compliance status. Begin the renewal process at least 30 days before your certification expiration to avoid gaps in your advertising authorization. A lapse in certification typically results in immediate suspension of your ads on all participating platforms.
How LegitScript Affects Your Facility
LegitScript certification primarily affects your marketing and admissions operations. Here is what operators need to know.
Digital Marketing Activation. The most immediate impact of LegitScript certification is enabling paid advertising on Google, Facebook/Meta, and Microsoft Bing. Work with your marketing team or agency to set up advertising accounts, create campaigns, and launch ads promptly after receiving certification. Each platform has its own account setup and ad approval process on top of LegitScript certification.
Website Content Audit. Before applying, review your website content against LegitScript’s standards. Remove or revise any content that makes unsubstantiated claims about treatment success rates, guarantees outcomes, uses deceptive testimonials, or otherwise violates healthcare advertising ethics. Your website is a key part of the certification review and ongoing monitoring.
Marketing Team Education. Ensure your marketing staff and any external agencies understand the advertising restrictions that come with LegitScript certification. Ad copy must be truthful and compliant. Landing pages must accurately represent your services. Violations can result in certification suspension, which would immediately shut down your paid advertising across all certified platforms.
Admissions Pipeline Integration. With digital advertising enabled, your admissions team needs processes in place to handle increased inquiry volume. Ensure your phone lines are adequately staffed, your admissions workflow can accommodate web leads, and your team can respond promptly to online inquiries. The value of digital advertising is wasted if leads are not converted efficiently.
Prerequisite Maintenance. Because LegitScript requires clinical accreditation and state licensing as prerequisites, allowing either to lapse will jeopardize your LegitScript certification and, by extension, your digital advertising capability. Build license and accreditation renewal tracking into your compliance calendar to ensure no gaps.
Competitive Positioning. In markets where many treatment centers compete for the same search terms and social media audiences, the quality of your advertising matters as much as your ability to run ads at all. LegitScript certification levels the playing field by ensuring all advertisers meet minimum legitimacy standards, but differentiating your facility still depends on compelling messaging, strong landing pages, and an excellent admissions experience.
Reputation Management. LegitScript certification is a verifiable trust signal. Display your LegitScript certification badge on your website and reference your certified status in your marketing materials. In an industry where trust is hard-earned, third-party verification of your legitimacy provides meaningful differentiation.
How Behave Health Helps
Behave Health’s CRM module supports the admissions pipeline that LegitScript-enabled digital advertising feeds, helping your team track and manage inquiries from Google Ads, Facebook campaigns, and Bing advertising. By connecting digital marketing leads to your admissions workflow, Behave Health helps ensure that the investment in LegitScript certification translates into actual admissions.

What It Really Takes for Weight Loss & Longevity Clinics to Get LegitScript-Certified: A Candid Q&A with White Label MD

As demand for GLP-1 and longevity care surges, LegitScript certification has become the gate to the two things every telehealth clinic depends on: advertising and payments. Having guided 250+ clinics through the process, White Label MD’s compliance team answers the questions founders actually need answered.
testimonial-whitelabelmd-logo
June 19, 2026 | by LegitScript Folks
A conversation with  
Justin Champion, CEO,  
White Label MD.
Justin Champion from White Label MD
Licensure is one of the first things LegitScript reviews. For weight loss and longevity clinics, that means being licensed in every state where a patient is located, not just where the clinic operates. Where do clinics most often discover a gap, and how costly is it to close?
The most common gap is geographic, and it comes from a wrong assumption. Founders think they need to be licensed where their clinic or their provider sits. But in telehealth, the law that governs care is the law of the state where the patient is located at the time of the visit. So a clinic running national ads with providers licensed in three states is, in practice, accepting patients it can’t legally treat in the other 47.
Closing it isn’t quick or cheap. Credentialing a provider in a new state takes time and money for each state, and licensing boards move at their own pace. The clinics that avoid the scramble decide their service-state map before they spend a dollar on ads, and build provider coverage to match.
GLP-1 demand brought a surge of clinics prescribing through both asynchronous and questionnaire-only models. LegitScript Certification requires licensed providers to deliver care before any prescription is issued. How does that play out for telehealth-first clinics, and what does a compliant care model actually look like?
The standard is easy to state and easy to get wrong: A licensed provider has to actually evaluate the patient and make the prescribing decision before any prescription is issued.
Asynchronous care can absolutely meet that bar. A provider reviewing a detailed intake, labs, and history and then making a real clinical judgment is legitimate telemedicine in most states. What doesn’t pass is the questionnaire-only model where a patient fills out a form and a prescription is generated with no genuine provider review, or where the “review” is a rubber stamp. Some states also require a synchronous video or phone component for certain prescriptions.
A compliant model has a real provider in the loop, documented clinical decision-making, and state-by-state logic for when a live visit is required. If your model only works because no one is actually practicing medicine, it won’t survive certification or an audit.
LegitScript’s affiliate and partner standards require pharmacy partners to be certified or accredited, and that flows upstream to the clinic. How often does a partner pharmacy become the obstacle that stalls an application?
More often than founders expect. LegitScript’s standards extend to your affiliates, and your pharmacy is the biggest one. If your fulfillment pharmacy isn’t appropriately licensed and accredited, or carries its own compliance baggage, that becomes your problem, and it can stall or sink an otherwise clean application.
We see founders choose a pharmacy on price, turnaround, or willingness to work with compounded GLP-1, without vetting the compliance side at all. By the time it surfaces in review, they’re weeks in and have to re-paper a core part of their supply chain. Vetting the pharmacy partner before you build around them is one of the highest-leverage moves a founder can make.
In the competitive weight loss and longevity markets, advertisers often use aggressive techniques. What are the most common transparency pitfalls clinics walk in with, and how do you clean them up?
This category attracts aggressive marketing, and that’s exactly where applications get flagged. The usual culprits: outcome claims that imply guaranteed or typical results, efficacy claims about the medication that go beyond what’s substantiated, before-and-after imagery without context, and pricing that hides the real subscription terms.
LegitScript wants advertising that’s truthful, substantiated, non-deceptive, and from a website that actually matches the ads. Cleaning it up means walking outcome promises back to what’s defensible, adding the right disclaimers, making pricing and cancellation terms unmissable, and aligning landing pages with ad copy. It’s less about neutering the marketing and more about making every claim one you can stand behind.
As part of the LegitScript Certification application process, applicants must provide full disclosure of disciplinary history for the business, its principals, and affiliated practitioners going back 10 years. For a white-label model with multiple providers, does that make the process more complex? What happens when something surfaces mid-application?
This is where the white-label model adds real complexity. The disclosure isn’t just about the business. It covers principals and affiliated practitioners, going back a decade. When care is delivered by a network of providers, that’s a lot of histories to surface and stand behind.
The work is front-loaded due diligence: know your providers’ and partners’ records before you submit, rather than discovering them in review. When something does surface mid-application — a past board action, a lapsed license, a prior business issue — it’s not automatically disqualifying, but it has to be disclosed and contextualized honestly. What sinks applications usually isn’t the issue itself; it’s the appearance of hiding it.
One of the main reasons clinics pursue LegitScript Certification is access to advertising on Google, Meta, and other platforms. What does responsible advertising look like post-certification?
The most important thing to note is that certification isn’t a license to say anything. It’s the start of an ongoing, monitored relationship. Responsible advertising post-certification means claims stay substantiated, pricing stays transparent, and your ads, landing pages, and actual service stay aligned.
It also means living inside the platforms’ own healthcare advertising policies, which are stricter than the law in places, and not drifting back into the aggressive claims that got the category scrutinized to begin with. The clinics that keep both their certification and their ad accounts treat compliance as a standing discipline, not a one-time gate they cleared.
For a founder just deciding whether to pursue LegitScript Certification, what’s the single biggest misconception they’re carrying and what do you wish they knew before starting?
It’s that certification is NOT a paperwork exercise — something you apply for, pay for, and receive. It isn’t. LegitScript verifies that your operation is genuinely compliant: your licensure, your clinical model, your pharmacy, your marketing, your data practices. You can’t paper over a model that doesn’t hold up.
The founders who struggled with the process built the business first and treated compliance as a final step to bolt on. The ones who breeze through prioritize compliance from day one. What I wish more founders knew: The application doesn’t make you compliant, it checks whether you already are.
Weight loss clinics collect sensitive patient data, including weight history, lab results, and medication records. How prepared are most applicants on privacy and data security, and where do the gaps appear?
This is consistently the most underprepared area. Founders focus on providers and pharmacy and treat data as an afterthought, despite handling incredibly sensitive PHI and PII.
The gaps we see most: missing business associate agreements with vendors who touch patient data, privacy policies that don’t reflect what the clinic actually does, no documented security safeguards, and no real breach-response plan. HIPAA isn’t a checkbox; it’s an operating posture. The clinics that are ready for certification treat data protection as infrastructure, not legalese, and it shows in how smoothly that part of the review goes.
LegitScript requires clinics to clearly disclose which states and territories they serve. For a clinic that wants to grow quickly, how does that shape launch strategy and what’s the risk of moving faster than licensure allows?
You have to disclose exactly which states you serve, and that disclosure has to match reality. The risk for a growth-minded founder is serious: It’s tempting to flip on national advertising and sort out licensure later, but accepting or prescribing for a patient in a state where you’re not licensed is a real violation, not a technicality.
So licensure has to lead expansion, not trail it. Practically, that means launching in the states you’re covered in, expanding licensure deliberately, and gating your marketing to your actual footprint. Growing faster than your licensure is one of the fastest ways to turn a promising clinic into an enforcement problem.
Compounded semaglutide became a flashpoint in 2024 and 2025, with the FDA’s position shifting and many clinics caught in a gray area. How do you advise clinics navigating drugs in regulatory uncertainty?
This is the hardest terrain in the category right now. Compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide expanded largely because the brand drugs were on the FDA shortage list, and as those shortages resolved, the legal footing for routine compounding narrowed and the FDA’s posture shifted.
The honest advice: Don’t build a business whose survival depends on a regulatory gray area. We tell founders to operate within current FDA guidance, work with qualified regulatory counsel, document the clinical basis for any compounded prescribing, and have a plan for branded medications so a single rule change doesn’t end the business overnight. The clinics that get hurt are the ones who bet everything on the gap staying open.
White Label MD promises a 30-day launch. Where does certification fit, parallel or first? And realistically, how long does it take for a well-prepared applicant?
It runs in parallel, but it has to start early. Review takes weeks, so we kick it off near the front of the launch, not the end to ensure that the platform, the clinical model, the pharmacy, and the marketing are all built to be certification-ready as we go, rather than retrofitted afterward.
For a well-prepared applicant, which includes complete documentation, licensure that matches the service map, a vetted pharmacy, a compliant site, review typically runs about two weeks. The reason most clinics take three or four months isn’t the review itself; it’s the back-and-forth of deficiency notices when they applied before they were ready. Doing it in parallel, and prepared, is the whole reason a 30-day launch is realistic.
LegitScript Certification unlocks both advertising and payment processing permissions, but is also the single most common place telehealth founders stall. White Label MD has guided 250+ clinics through it, and manages the entire process as part of a 60-day launch.

LegitScript Healthcare obtiene el reconocimiento de Google para su certificación de comerciantes en beneficio de los proveedores de telemedicina en España

Business Wire
4 min de lectura
 GOOGL
Con esta ampliación, los proveedores de telesalud en España ya disponen de una vía clara y fiable para anunciarse en las plataformas, a medida que crece el mercado de la telesalud en el país
PORTLAND, Oregón, July 25, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--LegitScript, líder en certificación y supervisión de los comerciantes y los productos en los sectores de la publicidad, el comercio electrónico y los pagos, ha anunciado hoy una ampliación de su colaboración con Google para certificar a los proveedores de telemedicina en España. Con la actualización de la política, que entrará en vigor el 5 de agosto de 2026, las empresas de telemedicina que operan en esta jurisdicción podrán solicitar la certificación LegitScript Healthcare y promocionar sus servicios en las plataformas publicitarias de Google.
Esto genera nuevas oportunidades para los proveedores de telemedicina en España y se produce tras las recientes ampliaciones de la certificación de LegitScript en la India y Nueva Zelanda, el Reino Unido, así como en Indonesia y Filipinas.
España se destaca gradualmente como mercado clave para la salud digital en Europa y se estima que su sector de telesalud crecerá a una tasa compuesta anual (CAGR) del 11,6 % entre 2026 y 2033. Acompañando el aumento la demanda, la ampliación de la colaboración de LegitScript con Google contribuirá a promover una publicidad en línea más segura para los servicios sanitarios y permitirá una publicidad de telemedicina que cumpla con la normativa en el mercado.
"Gracias a nuestra colaboración con Google, les ofrecemos a los proveedores de telemedicina de todo el mundo una vía más segura para hacer publicidad en línea", afirmó Jaylene Kunze, directora de operaciones y finanzas de LegitScript. "La implementación de nuestro programa de certificación en España representa un progreso importante en nuestra misión de ayudar a los proveedores a demostrar su cumplimiento normativo, anunciarse de forma responsable y generar confianza en los pacientes".
La Certificación Sanitaria de LegitScript les ofrece a las empresas de telemedicina una vía confiable, clara y en etapas para demostrar su cumplimiento normativo y su transparencia. Este proceso abarca la presentación de una solicitud, el envío de documentación para verificar la licencia y la legitimidad de la empresa, y la garantía del cumplimiento de las normas de privacidad de los pacientes, prácticas clínicas e integridad en el marketing. Si bien los proveedores de España ya podían solicitar la certificación de LegitScript, la actualización de la política de Google supone la primera vez que dicha certificación se reconocerá como parte del proceso de aprobación publicitaria de Google para los proveedores en España.
"La demanda mundial de servicios de telemedicina sigue en aumento y por eso, los proveedores necesitan vías seguras para llegar a los pacientes en línea y anunciarse de forma responsable", señaló Angela Salter, vicepresidente de Ventas y Alianzas de Certificación Empresarial de LegitScript. "Gracias a nuestra tecnología, nuestros datos propios y nuestra experiencia humana, la certificación de LegitScript les permite a los proveedores generar credibilidad, conectar con más pacientes a través de la plataforma publicitaria de Google y adaptarse a una normativa sanitaria en rápida evolución".
Para saber más sobre el programa de certificación sanitaria de LegitScript, descargar la lista de verificación de la solicitud e iniciar el proceso de solicitud, visite:
Para más detalles sobre las políticas publicitarias de Google y mantenerse al día de cualquier cambio, visite la página de inicio del Registro de cambios en las políticas publicitarias de Google.
Acerca de LegitScript
LegitScript, líder mundial en soluciones para gestionar los riesgos empresariales, cuenta con la confianza de los motores de búsqueda, los mercados de comercio electrónico, los proveedores de servicios de pago y las plataformas de redes sociales más importantes del mundo. Al combinar tecnología avanzada con la inteligencia artificial y una profunda experiencia en el sector, con una información de mercado cuidadosamente seleccionada, LegitScript permite a las empresas adelantarse a las amenazas emergentes y aprovechar nuevas oportunidades de crecimiento con precisión y rapidez. Nuestro equipo mundial de expertos en normativa y analistas es especialista en comprender los cambios normativos a nivel mundial y evaluar el riesgo en productos, sitios web, comerciantes y plataformas, para ofrecerles a los clientes una precisión inigualable, información útil y un apoyo excepcional.

What's Rarely Measured Matters Most
1190: Fixing What Growth Tries to Hide |  Jaylene Kunze, LegitScript
1190: Fixing What Growth Tries to Hide | Jaylene Kunze, LegitScript
When Jaylene Kunze was asked to help rebuild a struggling subsidiary in the United Kingdom, she packed up her family and moved overseas with her nine-month-old daughter. The assignment was one more example of the type of challenge that would come to define her career. Rather than following a traditional finance path, Kunze gravitated toward what she calls “the fixer” role, stepping into situations where businesses needed operational repair, process improvement, or organizational change.
That mindset began to take shape through compliance and Sarbanes-Oxley work. While many viewed the documentation requirements as burdensome, Kunze tells us the process forced her to understand “the intersection of people, process, and systems” behind the numbers. It gave her visibility into how businesses actually operated and prepared her for increasingly complex leadership roles.
Read More
Her appetite for transformation became especially valuable when Tendril transitioned from venture-capital ownership to private-equity ownership. Kunze tells us the company ultimately combined six businesses into what became Uplight. As CFO, she oversaw diligence and integration while helping absorb five acquisitions within seven months.
The experience delivered lasting lessons. Culture, she tells us, matters more than many leaders expect. Different organizations often make decisions in entirely different ways, creating friction that financial models cannot predict. She also learned the cost of pushing too hard. Her team successfully completed aggressive integrations, but Kunze tells us she underestimated the human toll and would invest more heavily in staffing and support if given the opportunity again.
Today, those lessons continue to shape how she approaches leadership, growth, and change.

CFOTL: Tell us about LegitScript. What’s this company about?
Kunze: LegitScript is a really cool company. It’s mission-based, and our mission is to make the internet and the payments ecosystem safer. What does that mean? It means we’re looking for the bad actors—people who are selling, transacting, or producing illegal goods and services on the internet.
We focus primarily on high-risk areas such as online pharmacies, telemedicine, firearms, gambling, and adult-related businesses. We work with major platforms like Google, payment providers, banks, credit card companies, and individual businesses to identify bad actors and help remove them from the ecosystem, preventing them from processing payments or advertising online.
Read More
To make it more tangible, many people know someone who uses a med spa or takes a GLP-1 weight-loss medication. One of our business lines focuses on certifying those who sell medicine online and ensuring they are legitimate pharmacists, licensed physicians, or sourcing medications from certified pharmacies. Ultimately, it’s about protecting consumers and helping ensure they receive legitimate products and services.
CFOTL: Tell us a little about the company’s capital structure over time. Could you share some of that history?
Kunze: The company was founder-built and founder-owned. The founder eventually sold the business to private equity, and today we’re operating under our second private-equity ownership cycle.
CFOTL: If you had to boil it down, what’s driving growth inside the business today?
Kunze: There are a few drivers. First, AI is making it easier to be a bad actor. You can spin up a website and appear to be selling legitimate products in a matter of minutes. As a result, the need for organizations that can identify bad actors and help remove them from the ecosystem continues to grow.
Another major driver is the continued expansion of telemedicine and telehealth since COVID. A significant portion of healthcare interactions now occur virtually. That creates a need for stronger controls and certification processes to ensure providers are legitimate and consumers are receiving real healthcare services and authentic medications.
CFOTL: We always like to ask about metrics. What are the input metrics you watch most closely?
Kunze: There are several. As a SaaS business, we monitor the standard metrics such as gross retention, net retention, and overall growth. What’s particularly important for us is that we operate three distinct product lines, so I spend a great deal of time evaluating product-line performance.
Product-line reporting is much harder than many people realize. This is probably the fifth company where I’ve worked to build reporting that goes beyond contribution margin and all the way down to understanding what each product line contributes to the bottom line. Each of our product lines is at a different stage of its lifecycle. One is growing very quickly, one is relatively stable, and another is dealing with pricing pressure.
That creates important resource-allocation decisions. We don’t want to starve a fast-growing product line in order to support another area unnecessarily. A significant part of my focus is understanding those tradeoffs, evaluating performance at the product-line level, and making sure we’re investing resources where they’ll create the greatest long-term value.

LegitScript Certification Applications Rise 59%, Led by 101% Growth in Telemedicine

Certification demand rises as telehealth expands into new care areas and providers look to compliance to support growth.
September 22, 2026 9:00 AM Eastern Daylight Time
PORTLAND, Ore. — (BUSINESS WIRE) — LegitScript, the leader in merchant and product certification and monitoring in the advertising, e-commerce, and payment sectors, today announced continued momentum across its certification program as behavioral health, telehealth, and other areas of digital healthcare continue to grow and evolve.
Over the past year, LegitScript has seen a 59% increase in certification applications overall and a 101% increase in telemedicine applications specifically. The growth comes as telehealth has expanded into a much broader ecosystem of providers, infrastructure platforms, and specialty healthcare companies, creating new ways for businesses to reach patients and grow.
“We’re seeing companies think about certification earlier than they used to,” said Scott Roth, CEO of LegitScript. “When you’re building a business, you want to know from the start that you’ll be able to advertise, accept payments, and reach the people you serve. More companies are recognizing that compliance needs to be part of that foundation.”
That demand is translating into continued certification growth, with total certifications up 43% over the past year and telemedicine certifications up 80%. LegitScript also recently surpassed 10,000 certified websites across healthcare, addiction treatment, and other highly regulated industries.
Telehealth is also expanding the types of care that can be delivered virtually, with behavioral health offering one example of how care models are changing. LegitScript has seen that growth firsthand, with Addiction Treatment Certifications up 80%. Mental health providers are adding substance use disorder treatment services, substance use disorder treatment providers are expanding into broader behavioral health, and new models are emerging to address both. That is happening alongside significant growth in the broader behavioral health market, which is projected to grow from $185.03 billion in 2025 to $332.77 billion by 2034.
“As providers add services, launch new models, and enter new markets, they can also encounter different regulatory requirements, advertising policies, and payment considerations”, said Jaylene Kunze,  Chief Operating and Financial Officer of LegitScript. “Addressing those requirements earlier can help make compliance part of the growth process rather than something businesses must revisit later.”
“We're seeing telehealth expand into categories that barely existed as virtual care options a few years ago," said Dr. Marc Serota, Founder and CEO of MD Integrations, a leading white-label telehealth platform. "As brands launch new services and move into new areas of care, certification gives them a clear, defined path instead of another unknown to navigate while they scale.”
As healthcare models continue to change, LegitScript is continuing to evolve its certification program and work with partners to meet the needs of growing businesses while maintaining the standards relied on by platforms, payment providers, and other stakeholders across the digital healthcare ecosystem.
LegitScript will be at the Behavioral Health Tech Conference in Nashville, Tennessee, September 22–24, at Booth #730 to discuss the changing digital healthcare landscape and the role of certification in supporting growth.

Definition
What LegitScript certification is
LegitScript reviews businesses in categories where fraud and patient harm are common. Its healthcare programs cover areas such as drug and alcohol addiction treatment, online and mail-order pharmacies, and some telehealth and healthcare merchant categories. Applicants submit details about the business, its owners and key staff, licenses and accreditations, websites and the services it offers. LegitScript checks these against legal requirements and its own standards, and then monitors certified businesses over time.
Certification is not a government license, and it does not replace state licensing or accreditation. Its practical value comes from the platforms that rely on it. Google uses it for addiction services advertisers in the US and accepts it for online pharmacy certification. Meta requires certification for advertisers in some regulated categories, such as online pharmacies and addiction treatment, and accepts LegitScript certification for this. Some payment processors also use it to decide whether to work with a merchant.
In marketing
How it applies to practice marketing
 Addiction treatment centers, detox and many IOP programs generally need certification before running Google or Meta ads for those services.
 Telehealth practices prescribing medications and pharmacies selling online should check whether their category requires it on each platform.
 Plan the timeline: the review can take weeks, so start before a launch date, not after ads are disapproved.
 Align the website: reviewers look at the same pages as patients. Claims, licenses, ownership details and policies must match the application.
 Apply on each platform: after certification, advertisers usually still apply to Google or Meta for the category.
See the LegitScript certification guide, the Google Ads healthcare policy guide and addiction treatment center marketing.
Limits
Common mistakes and limits
Certification is ongoing. Adding a location, changing ownership or launching a new site without updating the record can put certification and ad accounts at risk. Another mistake is assuming certification approves every ad. Platforms still review each ad and landing page against their own policies, and claims must still meet FTC and state rules.
Many ordinary practices, such as dental, dermatology or primary care, do not need LegitScript certification to advertise their services. Which categories require it, and the fees involved, change over time and differ by platform and country. Confirm current requirements on the platform's policy pages and with your compliance team before you apply.

FAQ
Common questions
Who needs LegitScript certification?
Typically drug and alcohol addiction treatment providers that want to advertise on Google or Meta in the US, online pharmacies, and some telehealth, supplement or other high-risk healthcare merchants. Requirements depend on the platform and category, so check each platform's current policy.
Do medical or dental practices need LegitScript to run Google Ads?
Usually not. Most practices advertising consultations and procedures do not need it. Certification becomes relevant for addiction treatment, online pharmacy, prescription drug promotion and certain telehealth offers, depending on the platform.
Is LegitScript certification a legal requirement?
No. It is a private certification. Platforms such as Google and Meta, and some payment processors, require it for certain categories. Businesses still have to meet state licensing, federal law and accreditation rules separately.
Does LegitScript certification guarantee ads will be approved?
No. After certification, advertisers usually still apply to the platform for the category, and each ad and landing page is still reviewed against the platform's policies. Misleading claims can be disapproved even for certified advertisers.

Compliance Alert: New Payment Regulations Affecting Clinics with Medication and Supplement Sales
TLDR - What You Need to Know
 Newly released enforcement policies from card networks like Visa and Mastercard have dramatically tightened the compliance requirements for independent practices around how prescription and pharmacy-grade products are paid for.
 Payment processors will need to move to enforce these new guidelines - which could cause a significant disruption in your services, if you are not compliant.   
+ In-Clinic Medication Sales must be processed using chip-enabled (EMV) terminals. Swiped or keyed card payments for prescription or pharmacy-only products are no longer compliant and can trigger processor shutdowns.
+ Online or Card-Not-Present Sales of medications (e.g., phone, invoice, website) now require LegitScript certification or recognized pharmacy accreditation. This includes selling GLP-1s, HRT, peptides, or compounded meds.   
Mastercard registration is mandatory for all online medication sales—no exceptions.
Note that taking online payment for a medication that is subsequently shipped by the pharmacy is also considered risky and non-compliant with most payment processors.
 To stay compliant, clinics should either:   
+ Ensure all in-person med sales are processed through an EMV terminals.
+ Or, bill only for services and have a pharmacy handle the medication sale directly.
Note - given the changing regulatory landscape, not all payment processors have started enforcing these new regulations! That said, non-compliance with any processor puts your clinic at risk of payment disruptions, account termination, and revenue loss.
If your clinic dispenses or sells medications, whether it’s GLP-1s for weight loss, testosterone for HRT, ketamine for mental health, or IV therapy injectables, it’s critical to pay attention to the shifting rules in the payment processing world.
New enforcement policies from card networks like Visa and Mastercard, along with updated guidelines from major processors, are tightening the compliance standards around how prescription and pharmacy-grade products are paid for.
And here’s the bottom line: How you collect payment for medications, both in person and online, can now directly affect your ability to stay active with your payment processor.
Let’s break down the two most critical compliance issues affecting clinics like yours today:
1. In-Clinic Medication Sales Must Be EMV (Chip) Terminal-Based
If your clinic dispenses or administers medications during a face-to-face visit, card-present transactions using a chip-enabled (EMV) terminal are now considered mandatory by most compliant processors.
This includes:
 Administering semaglutide, tirzepatide, or lipotropic injections for weight loss
 Dispensing bioidentical hormone creams or testosterone injections for hormone replacement therapy (HRT)
 Providing ketamine lozenges or nasal sprays
 Sending patients home with nutraceutical packs or compounded meds
Why it matters:
 Fraud Protection: EMV terminals drastically reduce the risk of payment fraud.
 Policy Alignment: Manually keyed or swiped payments for medication raise red flags, especially when the product is prescription-only or regulated.
 Processor Compliance: Many processors now require clinics to use EMV for any in-person medication sale—or risk being flagged or shut down.
Best Practice: Equip your front desk or checkout area with an EMV-capable terminal and ensure all staff are trained to use it for every in-person medication sale.
2. Selling Medications Online or by Phone? LegitScript May Be Required
If your clinic sells medications via phone, invoice, or your website, those transactions are classified as card-not-present and come with a completely different set of requirements.
To remain compliant with Mastercard and most modern processors, you must either:
 Be accredited as a pharmacy (see exceptions below), or
 Obtain LegitScript certification for your practice or site (note this certification is expensive and is likely out of reach for many providers starting their clinics).
This applies whether you're:
 Taking payments over the phone for refills of compounded thyroid meds
 Offering online reorders of IV supplements or injectables
 Running a membership program that includes monthly medication shipments
 Using e-commerce tools to sell prescription-weight loss medications
Even if you’re not advertising as an “online pharmacy,” the moment you sell prescription or pharmacy-grade products in a card-not-present transaction, these rules apply.
To avoid these rules, you may need to adjust your business model to take payment only for the services and not for the meds directly. More on that below!
Side Note: Accreditation Exceptions for Pharmacies
If your clinic includes a fully licensed pharmacy, you're exempt from LegitScript only if you're accredited through one of the following:
 National Association of Boards of Pharmacy (NABP)
 VIPPS, Vet-VIPPS, or VAWD programs
 LegitScript’s Merchant Certification Program
For non-pharmacy clinics offering compounded medications or in-office administered drugs, LegitScript is typically required for online or phone-based sales. Note: Mastercard registration is always required for medication sales online, regardless of your pharmacy status.
How This May Impact Your Business Model
This recent and sudden shift in payment compliance has real implications for how you structure your services and collect payments.
If your clinic isn’t structured as a pharmacy or LegitScript-certified provider, one compliant and increasingly popular model is to:
 Charge the patient for the clinical service (e.g., injection visit, treatment plan consultation)
 Send the prescription to a partner pharmacy, which then takes direct payment from the patient for the medication
This model protects your payment account, keeps you clear of regulatory pitfalls, and lets you focus on care delivery while your pharmacy partner handles the compliance-heavy sale of the medication.
Example: You charge for a weight loss consult that includes GLP-1 treatment planning. The semaglutide itself is fulfilled and charged separately by a pharmacy.
Alternatively, if you are dispensing medication on-site or bundling it into a treatment plan:
 Ensure your clinic has cards securely stored on file using a PCI-compliant gateway (OptiMantra’s payment processor integrations meet this requirement!)
 Always use EMV for in-person medication payments
 Clearly separate service and medication charges in your billing
 Don’t run card-not-present medication payments unless you’re certified to do so
Storing cards on file reduces no-shows, protects against chargebacks, and ensures smooth recurring billing for packages that include services and medications.
What You Can Do To Protect Your Business Now
1. Use chip-enabled (EMV) terminals for all in-clinic payments involving prescription or regulated products - check out Fiserv’s terminals (which can be rented or purchased)!
2. Avoid card-not-present medication sales unless you’re LegitScript certified or pharmacy-accredited
3. Evaluate your business model: Are you bundling meds into services and selling online without certification? Adjust your structure accordingly.
4. Implement card-on-file workflows to manage recurring payments and reduce risk
5. Talk to your processor: Make sure your business model, product list, and merchant category code (MCC) are fully transparent and accepted under their policies
Final Thoughts
As functional, integrative, and psychiatric care models evolve, so do the regulatory and operational demands. If you’re dispensing medications—whether for weight loss, HRT, mental health, or IV therapy—how you get paid matters more than ever.
Build a model that’s sustainable, compliant, and protects your business from unnecessary payment risk.

We support growing clinics in structuring compliant workflows and selecting payment partners that understand your model - we work closely with both Fiserv and Stripe which can help you get set up on payments. Our Payment Specialists are happy to answer any questions!

How Rapid Growth is Changing Telehealth Payment Processing
 Picture of Luqra   Luqra
Telehealth has gone from a niche service to one of the fastest-growing areas in healthcare. It was a useful, short-term solution during the pandemic, but now it’s a cornerstone of how millions of patients access medical care. From rural communities gaining access to the actual care they need, to busy professionals skipping waiting rooms, telehealth has become the preferred option for convenience, affordability, and accessibility.
The growth is staggering. The global healthcare digital payment market is projected to exceed $80 billion by 2033. That’s no trend, that’s an industry transforming in a matter of years. And like any transformation, it comes with new needs and new risks.
But what important detail do most telehealth companies still ignore? Payment processing.
Why Telehealth Is Growing So Quickly
Telehealth’s rise isn’t just about tech or the rise of the digital age. It’s about convenience, and it’s about need.
Several key forces have converged to push digital care into the mainstream:
 Increased Access: Patients in underserved or rural areas can now connect with providers without the barrier of distance.
 Lower Costs: Eliminating in-person visits reduces overhead for clinics and saves money for patients.
 Convenience and Flexibility: Scheduling around work, family, or emergencies is easier when appointments can happen anywhere.
 Tech Adoption: Mobile devices, faster networks, and better video platforms make real-time consultations seamless.
 Effects from the Pandemic:COVID-19 forced mass adoption of digital-first care, and many patients and providers never looked back.
This mix of access, cost savings, and necessity has cemented telehealth as a permanent fixture in modern healthcare.
The Unique Payment Needs of Telehealth Companies
Payment processing in telehealth isn’t just about swiping a card. It has to balance compliance, security, and seamless patient experience. Unlike retail or e-commerce, healthcare payments must adhere to strict regulations while remaining easy enough for patients to use without friction.
Some of the biggest priorities include:
 HIPAA Compliance: Patient health information (PHI) must remain secure during every transaction.
 PCI DSS Standards: Credit card information must be processed safely to avoid breaches.
 Recurring Billing: Many treatment plans involve repeat sessions. Auto-billing ensures continuity of care and reliable revenue.
 Flexible Payment Methods: From credit cards to ACH transfers, patients expect choice.
 Fraud and Chargeback Protection: Healthcare transactions are high-value and increasingly targeted by fraudsters.
In short, telehealth companies can’t afford to cut corners. The right payment processor doesn’t just handle transactions. It keeps your entire practice safe.
What Telehealth Companies Should Look for in a Payment Processor
Choosing a processor isn’t about who has the flashiest dashboard. It’s about finding a partner that understands the complex, high-risk nature of healthcare transactions and equips providers with the right tools.
Here’s what you really need from your processor:
1. HIPAA-Compliant Infrastructure
Not every processor can legally handle telehealth payments. If a processor doesn’t adhere to HIPAA standards, you’re exposing your business to lawsuits, fines, and reputational damage. Look for providers with built-in encryption, secure storage, and regulatory expertise.
2. Seamless Integration with Telehealth Platforms
Your payments should work inside the same systems you use for scheduling and consultations. Integration with existing EHR, telemedicine apps, or custom portals ensures providers don’t need to juggle multiple logins or patchwork tools. Patients also expect to pay inside the same portal where they book appointments.
3. Flexible Payment Options
ACH transfers, debit cards, credit cards, and even mobile wallets all need to be on the table. ACH is especially valuable for reducing costs compared to credit card processing, since it bypasses card networks and their high fees.
4. Recurring Billing & Invoicing
Treatment doesn’t end after one session. Patients often require ongoing care, and recurring billing makes that relationship easy to manage. Automated invoices, subscription-style payments, and customizable plans reduce missed payments and improve cash flow.
5.  Strong Fraud & Chargeback Protection
Fraud in telehealth isn’t just about stolen cards; it’s much broader than that. It can include disputes from patients who don’t recognize charges or misunderstand billing. Robust fraud prevention tools, blacklists, and chargeback defense mechanisms are non-negotiable.
6. High-Risk Merchant Expertise
Telehealth is often classified as a high-risk industry by banks and processors. That means more paperwork, slower onboarding, or even outright rejection if you pick the wrong partner. Processors experienced in healthcare know how to navigate underwriting, compliance reviews, and faster approvals.
7. Transparent Pricing
Hidden fees eat into margins. Telehealth providers need clear, predictable rates without being nickel-and-dimed for features like fraud monitoring or recurring billing.
8.  LegitScript Verification
Your payments should work inside the same systems you use for scheduling and consultations. Integration with existing EHR, telemedicine apps, or custom portals ensures providers don’t need to juggle multiple logins or patchwork tools. Patients also expect to pay inside the same portal where they book appointments.
How You Save With ACH Payments
One of the biggest shifts happening in telehealth is the ACH (Automated Clearing House) payments. Unlike transactions that pass through intermediaries, ACH transfers go directly from bank to bank.
That means payments are more sustainable, and they’re cheaper. For providers with large patient bases or subscription-style care models, those could be huge savings. ACH also helps patients by lowering service fees, making telehealth more affordable and easier to use.
Luqra: The Payment Partner Built for Telehealth Growth
Telehealth companies are in the business of making care easier and more accessible. Your payment processor should do the same.
At Luqra, we provide healthcare merchants with fully integrated payment solutions.
That means:
 HIPAA-compliant processing that prioritizes patient privacy.
 Direct ACH and card processing designed to reduce costs.
 Fraud detection tools built to protect both providers and patients.
 Custom-fit pricing that helps practices and businesses scale.
 LegitScript applications and onboarding that could be twice as fast and half the cost.
 24/7, In-House, and U.S.-based support that answers when you call.
Telehealth is here to stay, and the companies that thrive will be those that build trust—not just in their care, but in their financial systems. With Luqra, your payments are protected, optimized, and ready to scale with the future of digital healthcare.
